title: 54% of US Firefighters Are Volunteers
description:
Who fights the fires in your town? Maybe a volunteer.

Sources:
- BLS OEWS via api.bls.gov: Firefighters 33-2011, annual median wage, May 2025: https://api.bls.gov/publicAPI/v2/timeseries/data/OEUN000000000000033201113
- BLS OEWS via api.bls.gov: Firefighters, 10th percentile: https://api.bls.gov/publicAPI/v2/timeseries/data/OEUN000000000000033201111
- BLS OEWS via api.bls.gov: Firefighters, 90th percentile: https://api.bls.gov/publicAPI/v2/timeseries/data/OEUN000000000000033201115
- BLS OEWS via api.bls.gov: Firefighters, employment: https://api.bls.gov/publicAPI/v2/timeseries/data/OEUN000000000000033201101
- Wikipedia: Volunteer fire department: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volunteer_fire_department
- Wikipedia: Firefighting in the United States: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firefighting_in_the_United_States

NFPA (cited on Wikipedia): 54 percent of US firefighters are volunteers. US Department of Labor: volunteers get no pay or nominal fees up to 20% of a full-time firefighter's pay (Wikipedia). 95% of volunteer firefighters serve departments protecting fewer than 25,000 people (Wikipedia). BLS May 2025 (OEWS), paid firefighters: 345,990 jobs; median $59,280; 10th percentile $34,910; 90th percentile $101,040. Median = half earn more, half earn less. Not financial advice.

scenes.narration: Who fights the fires in your town? Maybe a volunteer.
Turns out, 54 percent of US firefighters are volunteers.
Their pay? Often nothing. Or just a small fee.
Most serve small towns. Still, they show up.
Only the paid ones get a salary. A median of 59,280 dollars.
